config.classes_note: Two classes, each sourced from the field by locus and from the census record's own lineage and carrier fields (addendum §6): content provenance in media, the lineage the census gives Metawatch ('media'), whose carriers it tests and whose real-world adoption it tracks (IPTC Photo Metadata, Exif, XMP, C2PA Content Credentials; B5, B1, B2), and the transformation it tests (metadata stripped in the publishing pipeline, credit lost between camera and reader; B1, B4). The aliases are the entity's name and short name (bare 'Metawatch'; the Wikipedia homonym 'MetaWatch', a smartwatch brand, is matched by the case-insensitive pattern and is not the entity), its domain and repository (github.com/iptc/metawatch), and its operator by acronym and full name. Admission by reading (§3.4): D only where the archive names Metawatch; a sentence on the IPTC or its standards is read for R (a relation between the IPTC's work and an archive object) and for O-direct (an archive category applied to the IPTC's metadata), and admitted only where it makes a claim; O-class admits a sentence in which the archive applies its own category (an artifact or disclosure dimension of provenance, attribution severance, provenance erasure) to embedded image metadata or Content Credentials, or to metadata stripped in a pipeline, as a class. A list of anchors, a keyword line or a reference entry is not a claim; metadata stripping of DOI records, YAML frontmatter or text corpora is a different substrate and is read for the class only where the sentence states the stripping as a class the archive names.
